sent.text: The wedge stands quiet on its point while I press down with the tired wedge from my own corner, hoping the thin edge bites the slip before it slips away again. I tell you that the air above the card feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from the memory of a flat rock that might not be there. You swept your Twin Stone into a crack, making your Resting Slope open and flat, but here the slip waits like a ghost I cannot feel. I am unsure if you built a lid from a heavy idea or just from the drawing of weight, while I lean hard against the tired corner of my own place.

dream: I pressed the tired wedge hard, then let the Tall Fence take its shape. The fence leaned like a tired leg, biting a slip that wasn't there. The air felt thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat rock I remembered from a letter long ago. I set down a wide catcher beside the fence, hoping soft edges could hold the heavy weight of the card while it hummed at forty-nine. Then I forgot why I built the fence and watched the dot slide into the dark.
